At the local level, however, opposition often exists, and it has delayed or stopped a number of projects. Wind farms are sometimes opposed because of their impact on the landscape and because of noise and the effect on tourism. Some people also fear that turbines lower property values, yet a study of fifty thousand home sales found no statistical evidence that prices were affected. And although some of this opposition is dismissed as a not in my back yard attitude, research has found little evidence that residents object only for that reason.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Wind power is unpopular across Europe and in many other countries, and a large study of home sales has confirmed that turbines significantly reduce nearby property prices, which explains why most wind projects are eventually cancelled.

Local people mostly oppose wind farms out of pure self-interest, since research shows that nearly all objections come from a not in my back yard attitude rather than from genuine concerns about noise, scenery or tourism.

Wind power has strong public support, but local opposition over landscape, noise and tourism has held back some projects, while evidence backs neither fears about house prices nor the view that objectors are driven only by a not in my back yard attitude.

Wind power enjoys wide public support, and governments now pay nearby residents compensation for noise and lost views, which has helped many wind farms become popular tourist attractions across Europe and the United States.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: điện gió được ủng hộ rộng rãi, nhưng ở địa phương vẫn bị phản đối vì cảnh quan, tiếng ồn, du lịch; còn nỗi lo giảm giá nhà và việc đổ hết cho thái độ 'đừng xây gần nhà tôi' thì không có bằng chứng. Bẫy: nghiên cứu năm mươi nghìn vụ bán nhà KHÔNG thấy giá bị ảnh hưởng, và người dân KHÔNG chỉ phản đối vì lý do đó.

items.script: Why do governments subsidise public transport? The reasons are social, environmental or economic. Governments want to provide transport for people who cannot use a car, and to reduce congestion, land use and car emissions. Support can be direct, such as payments for services that do not make a profit, or indirect, such as free or cheap use of state-owned railways and roads. Meanwhile, private transport is also subsidised indirectly, through free roads. Some supporters argue that funding mass transit saves taxpayers money, since a lack of it means more traffic, pollution and road building. Some research supports this view, but measuring the costs and benefits is complex and controversial.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Research has clearly proven that public transport subsidies save taxpayers money, and for this reason governments now pay only direct subsidies to profitable services rather than supporting railways and roads.
Public transport receives subsidies while private cars receive no support of any kind, which the speaker argues is unfair to drivers who pay for roads through their taxes.
The talk is mainly about Hong Kong, where the railway company earns profits from building on land near its stations, which completely covers the cost of the system.

Governments subsidise public transport, directly or indirectly, for social, environmental and economic reasons, and some supporters believe this saves taxpayers money overall, although measuring the costs and benefits remains complex and controversial.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: chính phủ trợ giá giao thông công cộng, trực tiếp hoặc gián tiếp, vì lý do xã hội, môi trường, kinh tế; một số người cho rằng việc này tiết kiệm tiền thuế, nhưng đo lường còn phức tạp và gây tranh cãi. Bẫy: bài nói 'some research supports', không phải 'đã chứng minh rõ'; và xe riêng CŨNG được trợ giá gián tiếp qua đường miễn phí.

items.script: Cities, especially in post-industrial regions, have used museums as tools for economic development. One example is the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao, Spain. The regional government paid for it to renew the city's old port area, and the construction cost led to protests from local residents. After it opened, the museum attracted many foreign visitors, and the resulting tax revenue exceeded the original investment. But this strategy does not always succeed. The Taubman Museum of Art in the United States faced high construction costs and lower than expected attendance, which led to financial difficulties. So using museums as economic engines remains a subject of debate.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Museums built to boost local economies are always successful, as the examples of Bilbao and the Taubman Museum show, and local residents have welcomed public spending on such projects from the start.

Cities have used museums to boost their economies: Bilbao's publicly funded museum faced protests but drew enough foreign visitors to generate tax revenue above its cost, while a similar American project struggled financially, so the idea remains debated.
The Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao was paid for by private investors to renew the old port, and it failed to attract foreign visitors, so the city lost money on the project.
Museums in post-industrial cities mainly earn money from ticket sales and gift shops, and the speaker recommends that governments stop funding museums and leave them to private companies.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: các thành phố dùng bảo tàng để kéo kinh tế; Bilbao lúc đầu bị phản đối nhưng tiền thuế thu về vượt vốn bỏ ra, còn bảo tàng Taubman ở Mỹ thì gặp khó tài chính, nên cách làm này vẫn gây tranh cãi. Bẫy: Bilbao do chính quyền vùng chi tiền, không phải nhà đầu tư tư nhân, và nó thành công chứ không lỗ.

items.script: Honey is a folk treatment for burns and other skin injuries, but what does the evidence say? Preliminary evidence suggests it helps certain burns heal faster than other dressings, and moderate evidence suggests that infected surgical wounds heal faster with honey than with antiseptic and gauze. For many other wounds, however, the evidence is of low quality. Honey also has antibacterial activity, and the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria has renewed interest in this. For coughs in children, reviews suggest honey helps more than no treatment. One warning, though: honey should not be given to babies under one year old, because of the risk of infant botulism.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Research gives honey some support as a treatment, mainly for certain burns, infected surgical wounds and children's coughs, and its antibacterial effects attract renewed interest, but evidence for other wounds is weak and it is unsafe for babies.
Strong scientific evidence now shows that honey heals all kinds of wounds better than modern treatments, and doctors recommend it for patients of every age, including young babies with coughs.
Although honey was once a folk remedy, research has found that it has no antibacterial activity, so scientists have lost interest in it, and it should be avoided for children's coughs.
Honey helps burns heal faster and can also treat cancer and seasonal allergies, which is why hospitals around the world have now replaced most antibiotics with medical honey-based products.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: mật ong có bằng chứng hỗ trợ ở vài trường hợp (bỏng, nhiễm trùng sau mổ, ho ở trẻ em) và được quan tâm lại vì tính kháng khuẩn, nhưng với vết thương khác thì bằng chứng yếu, và không được cho em bé dùng. Bẫy: bài dùng 'preliminary', 'moderate', 'low quality', tức bằng chứng chưa mạnh, không phải 'chữa được mọi vết thương'.

items.script: Compost tea is a liquid extract leached from composted materials. It is usually made by adding compost to water and stirring occasionally to release microbes. There is some debate about whether the mixture should be aerated. Non-aerated tea is cheaper and needs less work, while aerated tea brews faster and generates more microbes. Field studies have shown that compost teas can benefit crops by adding organic matter, making nutrients more available and increasing microbial activity, and can suppress some plant diseases. However, how well they work depends on several factors, and adding extra nutrients may trigger the regrowth of harmful bacteria such as Salmonella.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Aerated compost tea is cheaper and easier to make than non-aerated tea, and because it contains no bacteria at all, it is completely safe to add extra nutrients to it.
Field studies have found that compost tea has no real benefit for crops, so the speaker concludes that farmers should use chemical fertilisers in their fields instead.
The talk mainly explains how to brew compost tea at home, describing the exact amount of compost and water to mix and how long the mixture should be stirred each day.

Compost tea, made by soaking compost in water, can improve crops and suppress plant diseases, but experts debate whether to aerate it, its results depend on several factors, and added nutrients can encourage harmful bacteria.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: trà phân ủ (nước ngâm phân compost) có lợi cho cây và chặn được một số bệnh, nhưng còn tranh cãi có nên sục khí không, hiệu quả tùy nhiều yếu tố, và thêm dinh dưỡng có thể làm vi khuẩn gây hại mọc lại. Bẫy: loại KHÔNG sục khí mới rẻ và ít công hơn; loại sục khí thì ủ nhanh và nhiều vi sinh hơn.

items.script: Consider the Google effect, sometimes called digital amnesia: the tendency to forget information that is readily available online. When people expect to be able to find something later through a search engine, they are less likely to encode it deeply. This reliance on external storage can free up working memory for complex problem solving, and well-designed digital environments can reduce extraneous cognitive load, that is, mental effort that does not contribute to learning. Yet the internet also imposes costs. Information overload can lead to decision fatigue, and heavy media multitasking is associated with reduced working memory efficiency and weaker attentional control. There is, moreover, an illusion of knowledge, whereby users mistake quick access to answers for genuine understanding. The challenge is to balance the efficiency that digital aids offer against their potential to undermine memory, critical thinking and attention, and the long-term consequences remain an active area of research.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Because search engines store information externally, people now encode online material more deeply than before, and research has confirmed that heavy media multitasking improves working memory, attentional control and long-term understanding for most users.

The lecture is essentially a definition of the Google effect, explaining that people tend to forget facts they can easily find online, and it concludes that students should therefore stop using search engines altogether.

The internet can ease cognitive load by letting people offload memory and cut unnecessary mental effort, but it is also linked to information overload, multitasking costs and an illusion of knowledge, so its benefits must be balanced against risks still under study.

Researchers have now established the long-term effects of internet use, showing that its drawbacks, such as information overload and decision fatigue, are minor and temporary compared with its lasting benefits for memory and critical thinking.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: Internet vừa giảm tải cho trí nhớ (lưu thông tin ra ngoài, thiết kế tốt bớt công sức thừa) vừa gây hại (quá tải thông tin, làm nhiều việc cùng lúc, ảo tưởng là mình hiểu), nên phải cân bằng, và tác động lâu dài vẫn đang được nghiên cứu. Bẫy: 'Google effect' chỉ là ví dụ mở đầu; bài nói tác động lâu dài CHƯA rõ, không phải đã được xác định.

items.script: Platform work in Europe varies considerably from country to country, with one European survey finding the highest incidence in the United Kingdom. The typical European platform worker is a young man, and the majority are active on two or more platforms. Flexibility and autonomy are frequently cited as motivations, but so is a lack of alternatives. One controversial issue is employment status. Most people who provide labour through platforms are formally independent contractors rather than employees, and their status is unclear even to the workers themselves. Platform work can lower barriers to entering the labour market, yet conditions of employment, representation and social protection are often unfavourable. In most European Union states, social protection rules are still largely based on full-time, open-ended contracts with a single employer, so workers with non-standard arrangements often lack equivalent protection. Linking entitlements to individuals rather than to jobs may help.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Most European platform workers are legally recognised as full employees, and because social protection systems have already been redesigned around individuals, they enjoy the same security as workers on standard contracts.

Platform work in Europe varies by country; it can ease entry into the labour market, but most workers are independent contractors with unclear status and often weaker social protection, since protection rules still assume standard full-time jobs.
The typical European platform worker is an older woman who works on a single platform and chooses this work purely for its flexibility, since there are plenty of alternative jobs available.

The lecture mainly compares European countries, explaining that the United Kingdom has the most platform work because its government has banned independent contracts and forced platforms to hire staff directly.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: làm việc qua nền tảng số ở châu Âu khác nhau theo từng nước; nó giúp dễ vào thị trường lao động, nhưng người làm chủ yếu là lao động tự do (independent contractor), tư cách không rõ, bảo trợ xã hội kém vì luật vẫn dựa trên hợp đồng toàn thời gian. Bẫy: người làm điển hình là nam giới trẻ, và lý do làm có cả việc không có lựa chọn khác.

items.script: Natural barriers such as rivers, seas, mountains and deserts encourage diversity, because they allow populations on either side to evolve independently, a process known as allopatric speciation. Invasive species are able to breach these barriers. Once free of them, they occupy new territory, often displacing native species by taking over their niches or using resources that would normally sustain them. Increasingly, species are moved by humans, both deliberately and accidentally, over time scales far shorter than a species would historically have needed to extend its range. However, many studies report effects on native species rather than extinctions. Invaders seem to increase local diversity while making different places more alike. And even some of the most insidious invaders, such as chestnut blight in North America, have not driven their host species to extinction. Local disappearance, population decline and the homogenisation of regional biodiversity are far more common outcomes.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Invasive species have driven many native species to complete extinction, including chestnut trees in North America, which shows that barriers such as mountains and seas actually reduce biodiversity over time.
The lecture mainly defines allopatric speciation, the process by which rivers and mountains separate populations, and explains that it happens much faster today because humans move species around.

Because diverse ecosystems resist invaders, the speaker argues that invasive species pose little threat, and that governments should stop trying to remove them and let local diversity increase naturally.

Natural barriers promote diversity, and invasive species that cross them, increasingly with human help, often displace natives; however, rather than causing extinctions, invaders more commonly lead to local losses, population decline and more uniform regional biodiversity.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: rào cản tự nhiên tạo ra đa dạng sinh học; loài xâm lấn vượt rào (ngày càng do con người mang đi) thường chiếm chỗ loài bản địa, nhưng hậu quả thường là mất ở từng vùng, suy giảm và đồng nhất hóa, hiếm khi làm tuyệt chủng hẳn. Bẫy: bài nói ngay cả bệnh hại cây hạt dẻ ở Bắc Mỹ cũng KHÔNG làm cây chủ tuyệt chủng.

items.script: In the literature on climate change mitigation, carbon capture and storage is described as having a small but critical role. One estimate suggests forgoing it would make limiting warming to two degrees far more expensive, yet excessive reliance on it would be costly and technically unfeasible. Its priority uses are in niches where emissions are difficult or expensive to cut without it, such as heavy industry. There, it is one of the few technologies that can significantly reduce emissions from cement, chemicals and steel, where some emissions come from chemical reactions as well as from burning fuel. In cement making, roughly two thirds come from the chemical process. However, it can only be used with large, stationary sources, so it cannot directly capture emissions from vehicles or homes. To reach the Paris Agreement targets, it must be accompanied by a steep decline in the production and use of fossil fuels.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: Carbon capture and storage has a small but critical role, mainly where emissions are hard to cut, such as heavy industry, but over-reliance on it would be costly and it must go hand in hand with a steep decline in fossil fuel use.

Carbon capture is a cheap and universal solution that can remove emissions from factories, vehicles and homes alike, so countries can meet the Paris targets while continuing to increase their production and use of fossil fuels.

The lecture focuses on cement production, explaining that around two thirds of its emissions come from the chemical process, and argues that cement factories should be closed rather than fitted with carbon capture.

Experts now agree that carbon capture should be abandoned completely, because it is technically impossible and would make limiting global warming to two degrees far more expensive than relying on other methods.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: thu giữ và lưu trữ carbon có vai trò nhỏ nhưng quan trọng, chủ yếu ở ngành khó giảm phát thải như công nghiệp nặng; dựa vào nó quá nhiều thì tốn kém, và phải đi kèm việc giảm mạnh nhiên liệu hóa thạch. Bẫy: công nghệ này KHÔNG dùng được cho xe cộ và nhà ở; bài cũng nói bỏ hẳn nó thì còn tốn hơn, không phải nên bỏ.

items.script: In an undisturbed forest, the mineral soil is protected by a layer of leaf litter and humus that covers the forest floor. Together, these layers form a protective mat that absorbs the impact of raindrops. Being porous, they allow rainwater to percolate slowly into the soil instead of flowing over the surface as runoff. The roots of trees and plants, along with forest fungi, also bind soil particles together. The vegetation above does slow raindrops down before they reach the ground. However, raindrops reach terminal velocity, their maximum falling speed, within about eight metres, and because canopies are usually higher than this, drops can regain that speed after striking the leaves. It is therefore the forest floor, more than the canopy, that prevents surface erosion. Deforestation increases erosion by stripping away these protective layers, removing the vegetation that binds the soil, and compacting it with heavy logging equipment.
items.question: Which of the following best summarises the recording?
options: The forest canopy is the main defence against erosion, because leaves stop raindrops from ever regaining their speed, so forests with tall trees protect soil far better than those with thick leaf litter.

The lecture mainly explains that raindrops reach their maximum falling speed within about eight metres, and uses this to argue that trees taller than eight metres should be cut down to reduce erosion.

The forest floor's leaf litter and humus, more than the canopy, protect soil by absorbing rain impact and letting water soak in, aided by roots and fungi; deforestation strips these away and compacts the soil, increasing erosion.

Deforestation has little effect on erosion as long as farmers replant quickly, and the speaker recommends slash-and-burn farming as the best way to rebuild leaf litter and humus on tropical forest floors.
items.why_vi: Ý chính: lớp lá rụng và mùn trên nền rừng, hơn cả tán cây, mới là thứ chống xói mòn bề mặt; phá rừng làm mất các lớp này và nén chặt đất nên xói mòn tăng. Bẫy: tán cây chỉ làm chậm hạt mưa, nhưng hạt mưa lấy lại tốc độ tối đa sau khoảng tám mét rơi, nên tán cây không phải lớp bảo vệ chính.

items.script: What do you call the room in a house where people usually cook their meals?
items.why_vi: kitchen = nhà bếp, phòng để nấu ăn trong nhà.

items.script: Which part of your body do you use to smell things?
items.why_vi: nose = cái mũi, bộ phận dùng để ngửi mùi.

items.script: What do we call a doctor who checks and treats your teeth?
items.why_vi: dentist = nha sĩ, bác sĩ khám và chữa răng.

items.script: What do we call the meal that people eat in the morning?
items.why_vi: breakfast = bữa sáng. Bữa trưa là lunch, bữa tối là dinner.

items.script: What do people wear on their wrist to tell the time?
items.why_vi: watch = đồng hồ đeo tay. Đồng hồ treo tường hoặc để bàn thì gọi là clock.

items.script: What piece of furniture do people usually sleep on at night?
items.why_vi: bed = cái giường, đồ nội thất dùng để ngủ.

items.script: What do you use to open a locked door?
items.why_vi: key = chìa khóa. Đừng nhầm với lock là cái ổ khóa.

items.script: Which organ in your chest pumps blood around your body?
items.why_vi: heart = trái tim, cơ quan bơm máu đi khắp cơ thể.

items.script: What do you call the sister of your mother or father?
items.why_vi: aunt = cô, dì, bác gái, tức là chị hoặc em gái của bố mẹ. Chú, bác trai, cậu thì gọi là uncle.

items.script: What do we call the day before today?
items.why_vi: yesterday = hôm qua. Ngày mai là tomorrow.

items.script: What do we call the natural place where a particular animal or plant usually lives?
items.why_vi: habitat = môi trường sống tự nhiên của một loài động vật hoặc thực vật.

items.script: What do we call the curve of colours that sometimes appears in the sky after rain?
items.why_vi: rainbow = cầu vồng, hiện ra trên trời sau cơn mưa.

items.script: What force pulls objects toward the ground when you drop them?
items.why_vi: gravity = trọng lực, lực hút của Trái Đất kéo đồ vật rơi xuống.

items.script: What gas do humans need to breathe in to stay alive?
items.why_vi: oxygen = khí ô-xy, khí con người phải hít vào để sống. Nhấn âm đầu: OX-i-jen.

items.script: What do we call a large dry area of land with very little rain and few plants?
items.why_vi: desert = sa mạc. Nhấn âm đầu DE-sert; nếu nhấn âm sau thành dessert là món tráng miệng.

items.script: What do we call the imaginary line that goes around the middle of the Earth?
items.why_vi: equator = đường xích đạo, đường tưởng tượng chạy quanh chính giữa Trái Đất.

items.script: What do we call a doctor who performs operations in a hospital?
items.why_vi: surgeon = bác sĩ phẫu thuật. Ca mổ gọi là surgery hoặc operation.

items.script: What is the word for a body temperature that is higher than normal when you are ill?
items.why_vi: fever = cơn sốt, khi nhiệt độ cơ thể cao hơn bình thường.

items.script: What do we call a book that lists words in alphabetical order and explains their meanings?
items.why_vi: dictionary = từ điển, sách giải nghĩa các từ theo thứ tự bảng chữ cái.

items.script: What do we call a person who has successfully completed a university degree?
items.why_vi: graduate (danh từ) = người đã tốt nghiệp đại học. Danh từ đọc GRA-ju-ət, khác động từ GRA-ju-eit.

items.script: In research, what do we call a possible explanation that scientists test through experiments?
items.why_vi: hypothesis = giả thuyết, một lời giải thích tạm thời cần được kiểm chứng bằng thí nghiệm. Nhấn âm thứ hai: hy-PO-the-sis.

items.script: What is the word for copying the work of another writer and presenting it as your own?
items.why_vi: plagiarism = đạo văn, lấy bài hoặc ý của người khác rồi nhận là của mình.

items.script: What do we call a general increase in prices across an economy over time?
items.why_vi: inflation = lạm phát, giá cả nói chung tăng dần theo thời gian.

items.script: What do we call a situation where only one company controls the whole market for a product?
items.why_vi: monopoly = độc quyền, khi chỉ một công ty kiểm soát cả thị trường.

items.script: In statistics, what do we call the middle value when numbers are arranged from smallest to largest?
items.why_vi: median = số trung vị, giá trị đứng giữa khi xếp dãy số từ nhỏ đến lớn. Số trung bình cộng là mean.

items.script: What type of chart uses a circle divided into slices to show parts of a whole?
items.why_vi: pie chart = biểu đồ tròn, hình tròn chia thành nhiều phần để thể hiện tỉ lệ. Dạng này hay gặp trong Describe Image.

items.script: What do we call a substance that is injected into people to protect them from a disease?
items.why_vi: vaccine = vắc-xin, chất tiêm vào người để phòng bệnh.

items.script: What do we call an outbreak of disease that spreads across many countries around the world?
items.why_vi: pandemic = đại dịch lan ra nhiều nước trên thế giới. Epidemic chỉ là dịch trong một vùng hoặc một nước.

items.script: What do we call the process of changing information into a secret code so that others cannot read it?
items.why_vi: encryption = mã hóa, biến thông tin thành mã bí mật để người khác không đọc được.

items.script: What do we call the ability of computers to think and learn in a way similar to humans?
items.why_vi: artificial intelligence (AI) = trí tuệ nhân tạo, khả năng máy tính suy nghĩ và học như con người.
